title: Closest Race Times
statement: Runners' finishing times are given in seconds, in no particular order. Return the smallest gap between any two finishing times.

approaches.name: Sort, then scan
approaches.label: best
approaches.why: After sorting, the closest pair must be neighbors, so one scan over neighbors finds it.

approaches.name: Nested loops
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Checks every pair. Correct, but slow for 100,000 runners.

approaches.name: HashMap / HashSet
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: A set finds equal values fast, but not the nearest different value.

approaches.name: Single pass
approaches.hint: One loop with a running value
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: In the original order the closest times can be far apart, so one pass cannot compare them.

title: Runner-Up Score
statement: Given the scores of a contest, return the second-highest distinct score, or null if every score is the same.

approaches.name: Single pass
approaches.hint: One loop with a running value
approaches.label: best
approaches.why: Keep the highest and second-highest distinct values while scanning once.

approaches.name: Sort, then scan
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Sort, then walk down from the top until a smaller value appears. Correct, but sorting does more work than needed.

approaches.name: Nested loops
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: For each score, check whether exactly one distinct score is bigger. Correct, but slow.

title: Join Two Sorted Lines
statement: Two ticket counters each keep their customers' arrival times in increasing order. Return all arrival times as one increasing list.
constraints: Up to 100,000 times in each line

approaches.name: Merge with two fingers
approaches.label: best
approaches.why: Take the smaller front item each step; each time is moved once because both lines are already sorted.

approaches.name: Join, then sort
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Join the lines, then sort. Correct, but ignores that each line is already in order.

approaches.name: Insert one by one
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Inserting each time of one line into the other keeps order, but each insert can shift many items.

approaches.name: HashMap / HashSet
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: A hash set loses the order and drops repeated times.
